text.p: International Business Machines Corp announced a "SMART check" product which will give bank customers itemized statements grouping their expenditures by categories such as utilities, groceries, automotive and entertainment.

IBM said the product uses image recognition technology along with a new type of check that has small boxes on the left hand side where people can designate an expense category for a household or small business.

In a telephone interview, Geoff Emerson, director of IBM payment solutions, said the system is a time-saver for people who would no longer have to spend a couple hours weekly typing in data for a software program. "This allows the bank to do that for you," he said. "For a few dollars a month it's a very useful tool."
He said consumers would be able to tell at a glance how they were spending their money.

Emerson said banks that use the product could customize it as they saw fit. He said banks would also be able to integrate debit card transactions into the statement, and depending on the bank, let indivduals see their activity for the prior 12 months or the year-to-date.
